content:
Apple's major September event will be held this Wednesday, with the company set to unveil three brand-new iPhone models: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra. Here's what you can expect.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will succeed Apple's popular 17 Pro series.

Rumoured new features include:

  • The A20 Pro chip, delivering stronger performance and improved efficiency
  • Major camera upgrades, notably the addition of a variable aperture main lens
  • A 35% reduction in the size of the Dynamic Island, giving the design a more modern look
  • A new colour option, headlined by a bold burgundy
  • The best battery life ever, with the iPhone 18 Pro Max seeing a significant boost
  • A redesigned Camera Control button
  • Apple's in-house C2 cellular modem
  • New satellite features, including 5G satellite connectivity

The starting price of the iPhone 18 Pro is also expected to rise. Outside estimates put it at around US$1,399, but I think the real figure could be closer to US$1,199 or US$1,249.

iPhone Ultra

The iPhone Ultra is reportedly Apple's first foldable iPhone, with an expected price tag exceeding US$2,000, and will create an entirely new premium product line.

The foldable design makes the iPhone Ultra the most groundbreaking model Apple has released to date. It will adopt a wide book-style fold, with an outer display of roughly 5.4 inches and an inner display of 7.8 inches, similar to an iPad mini.

The design and materials are expected to follow the iPhone Air, featuring a titanium frame and a clean, minimalist look.

The iPhone Ultra will come with two rear cameras (main and ultra-wide) and two front cameras, one for each display. Authentication will be handled by Touch ID rather than Face ID.

Software will be the biggest highlight of this device, with iOS 27 enabling side-by-side app multitasking and adaptive landscape layouts, fully taking advantage of the all-new form factor.

Performance is expected to be on par with the iPhone 18 Pro, using the same A20 Pro chip, paired with a vapour chamber cooling system and the C2 modem.

The missing models: iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2

As usual, September typically sees the simultaneous launch of the all-new base-model iPhone 18 and the successor to the iPhone Air.

However, reports say Apple will significantly reshuffle its autumn lineup this year, pushing the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 back to an early 2027 release.

It remains unclear whether this shift is purely a strategic decision or a forced move driven by the current memory shortage. Either way, the absence of more affordable models means this autumn's new iPhone lineup will be focused firmly on the high-end market.

Are any of you planning to upgrade to a new iPhone this autumn? Which model will you go for? Feel free to share in the comments.
